newsitem.title: UK: Pre-Christmas bidding spree boosts UK stocks.
newsitem.headline: Pre-Christmas bidding spree boosts UK stocks.

text.p: A pre-Christmas bidding spree has boosted London stocks as companies go shopping for takeover targets, putting a price tag of more than 2.0 billion pounds ($3.3 billion) on their list of potential purchases.

Both home and overseas firms launched at least five major bids for British companies this week -- most of them hostile -- enlivening the normally dull holiday period for dealmakers and putting a damper on the holidays for reluctant bid targets.

Corporate financiers say the unusual end-of-the-year dash may be due to a perceived need to finish deals ahead of a possible change in government next year and a desire to take advantage of high stock prices.

"Markets tend to be reasonably buoyant in the new year, and so therefore, if you're relying on an equity funding, it's probably not a bad time," said Robert Swannell, head of UK corporate finance at Schroders.
London's top 100 blue chips gained 28.7 points to 4046.9 by 1430 GMT on Thursday.
Corporate financiers say the prospects of Britain's opposition Labour Party winning the next general election, due by May 1997, might also be a factor behind the recent spate of bids.
Labour, currently leading polls, has traditionally been viewed as a stricter regulator of industries and financial markets than the Conservative government.

"Clearly there is uncertainty about the policy of a Labour government. And if they are going to have a very different competition policy, then you'd probably be as well to get on with it now," Swannell said.
Potentially stricter regulation of utilities by a Labour Government may also be fuelling the bidding frenzy for Britain's few remaining independent regional electricity companies (RECs).
"With the RECs, I suspect there's an element of not wanting to be left out with a limited number of potential targets," Swannell said.

In one of the largest deals this week, U.S. group Entergy Corp finally agreed to a 1.27 billion pound offer for power supplier London Electricity on Wednesday, after talks between them were called off in November.
By launching their bids near the year-end, predator firms might also benefit from an "inconvenience factor" as takeover targets scramble to defend themselves during the holidays.

"It's a marginal inconvenience for the other side," Swannell said. "But generally, if companies are facing a hostile bid, they're prepared to give up their Christmas pudding for the company they work for."
Although bidding activity in the next couple of weeks is unlikely to match this week's flurry, corporate financiers say yet more British firms are likely to become bid targets in 1997.

"We certainly see the first quarter of next year being very active. There are a lot of transactions in the pipeline, a lot of activity," Rupert Faure Walker, head of corporate finance at HSBC Samuel Montagu, told Reuters.
Gulf Canada Resources Ltd's hostile 432 million pound bid for Britain's Clyde Petroleum on Wednesday highlighted the possibility of other bids in the energy sector.
Meanwhile, British drug stocks were still a perennial subject of market merger rumours, while the financial sector, particularly insurers, was also seen as ripe for consolidation.
Major bids and agreed offers for British firms launched this week, ranked according to estimated value of deal:
-- Entergy agreed to a 1.27 billion pound cash takeover of London Electricity on Wednesday.
-- Oil and gas company Gulf Canada Resources Ltd made a hostile 432 million pound cash offer for Britain's Clyde Petroleum on Wednesday.
-- British insurance brokers Lloyd Thompson Group Plc and JIB Group Plc agreed on Monday to merge in a stock deal worth 300 million pounds.
-- British engineering group FKI Plc launched a hostile share-and-cash bid for lock maker Newman Tonks Plc on Tuesday, valuing it at nearly 200 million pounds.

-- British electronics and specialist engineering firm Fairey Group Plc launched a hostile 51.1 million pound stock bid for Burnfield Plc on Tuesday. The bid also included a cash alternative. ($1=.5982 Pound)
